title: The Heart Sutra in Seven Translations
excerpt: The Heart Sutra has seven important translations: two abridged versions and five full versions. The so-called full version comprises the three major sections of the preface, the main teaching, and the concluding dedication; the abridged version contains only the main teaching.

inline.s: The Heart Sutra has seven important translations: two abridged versions and five full versions. The so-called full version comprises the three major sections of the preface, the main teaching, and the concluding dedication; the abridged version contains only the main teaching.
The two abridged versions:
1. The Maha-Prajna-Paramita Dharani Sutra (402-413 CE), translated by Kumarajiva of the Later Qin.
2. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra (649 CE), translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.
The five full versions:
1. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra of the Universal Wisdom Treasury (738 CE), retranslated by Fayue of the Tang dynasty.
2. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra (790 CE), jointly translated by Prajna and Liyan of the Tang dynasty.
3. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra (Dunhuang cave edition), translated by Facheng of the Tang dynasty.
4. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra (847-859 CE), translated by Zhihuilun of the Tang dynasty.
5. The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Prajna Paramita of the Holy Buddha-Mother (980-1000 CE), translated by Shihu of the Song dynasty.
Today the most popular translation is the one by the Great Master
Xuanzang
; the whole sutra runs to 260 characters.

blocks.text: 1. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra

inline.s: Translated by the Tang dynasty Tripitaka Master Xuanzang.
When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara was practicing the profound Prajna Paramita, he illuminated the five aggregates and saw that they were all empty, thereby overcoming all suffering and distress.

Sariputra! Form does not differ from emptiness, emptiness does not differ from form; form is emptiness, emptiness is form. The same is true of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Sariputra! All dharmas are marked with emptiness; they are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, neither increasing nor decreasing.

Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental object; no realm of sight, up to no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance, and no extinction of ignorance; up to no aging and death, and no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, no origination, no cessation, no path; no wisdom; and no attainment.

Because there is nothing to be attained, the Bodhisattva, relying on Prajna Paramita, has a mind without obstruction. Without obstruction there is no fear; having transcended all inverted dreams and views, he reaches ultimate Nirvāṇa.
The Buddhas of the three times, relying on Prajna Paramita, attained Anuttara Samyak Sambodhi.
Therefore, know that Prajna Paramita is the great god-mantra, the great illuminating mantra, the supreme mantra, the unequaled mantra, which can remove all suffering — this is true, not false.
Therefore, the mantra of Prajna Paramita is proclaimed. The mantra says: Gate! Gate! Paragate, Parasamgate, Bodhi Svaha!
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumarajiva of India under the Later Qin.
When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara was practicing the profound Prajna Paramita, he illuminated the five aggregates and saw that they were empty, thereby overcoming all suffering and distress.

Sariputra, because form is empty there is no mark of vexation and destruction; because feeling is empty there is no mark of feeling; because perception is empty there is no mark of cognition; because mental formations are empty there is no mark of activity; because consciousness is empty there is no mark of awareness.

Why? Sariputra, it is not that form is other than emptiness, nor that emptiness is other than form; form is emptiness, emptiness is form. The same holds for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Sariputra, all dharmas are marked with emptiness; they neither arise nor cease, are neither defiled nor pure, neither increase nor decrease. This empty dharma is neither past, nor future, nor present. Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental object; no realm of sight, up to no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance and no extinction of ignorance, up to no aging and death and no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, origination, cessation, or path; no wisdom; and no attainment.

Because there is nothing to be attained, the Bodhisattva, relying on Prajna Paramita, has a mind without obstruction. Without obstruction there is no fear; having distanced himself from all inverted dreams, views, and afflictions, he reaches ultimate Nirvāṇa.
The Buddhas of the three times, relying on Prajna Paramita, attained Anuttara Samyak Sambodhi.

Therefore, know that Prajna Paramita is the great illuminating mantra, the supreme illuminating mantra, the unequaled illuminating mantra, which can remove all suffering — this is true, not false. Therefore, the mantra of Prajna Paramita is proclaimed, and the mantra says:
Gate! Gate! Paragate, Parasamgate, Bodhi Svaha!

blocks.text: 3. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra of the Universal Wisdom Treasury

inline.s: Retranslated by the Tripitaka monk Fayue of the land of Magadha.

Thus I have heard. At one time the Buddha was dwelling at Vulture Peak in the great city of Rajagriha, together with a full thousand great monks and seventy-seven thousand Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas. Their names included the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the Bodhisattva Manjusri, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, and others, who were at the head of the assembly. All had attained the samādhi of dharanis and dwelt in inconceivable liberation.

At that time the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara was seated there. Rising from his seat in the midst of the assembly, he went to where the World-Honored One was, faced him with palms joined, bowed in reverence, and gazing upon the Blessed One's countenance, said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, I wish to speak in this assembly the Heart of Prajna Paramita of the Universal Wisdom Treasury of all Bodhisattvas. May the World-Honored One be pleased to hear my words and proclaim the profound essentials of the Dharma for the Bodhisattvas.

At that time the World-Honored One, with his wondrous Brahma-voice, said to the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Well said! Well said! O one endowed with great compassion, I hear your words; they shall be a great light for all beings.

Thereupon the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara, having received the Buddha's permission and being protected and remembered by the Buddha, entered into the samādhi of the light of wisdom. Having entered that concentration, by the power of the samādhi he practiced the profound Prajna Paramita and illuminated the five aggregates, seeing that their self-nature was all empty. Having understood that the five aggregates are empty in their self-nature, he arose calmly from that samādhi and addressed the wise Sariputra:

Good man, the Bodhisattva possesses the Heart of Prajna Paramita, named the Universal Wisdom Treasury. Listen attentively and consider it well; I shall expound it to you in detail. Having thus spoken, the wise Sariputra said to the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: O pure one, may it please you to speak; now is exactly the time.

Then he addressed Sariputra: All Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas should thus learn that the nature of form is emptiness, the nature of emptiness is form; form is not other than emptiness, emptiness is not other than form; form is emptiness, emptiness is form. The same holds for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. The nature of consciousness is emptiness, the nature of emptiness is consciousness; consciousness is not other than emptiness, emptiness is not other than consciousness; consciousness is emptiness, emptiness is consciousness.

Sariputra, all dharmas are marked with emptiness; they neither arise nor cease, are neither defiled nor pure, neither increase nor decrease. Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental object; no realm of sight, up to no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance, and no extinction of ignorance, up to no aging and death, and no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, origination, cessation, or path; no wisdom; and no attainment.

Therefore, know that Prajna Paramita is the great god-mantra, the great illuminating mantra, the supreme mantra, the unequaled mantra, which can remove all suffering — this is true, not false. Therefore, the mantra of Prajna Paramita is proclaimed, and the mantra says:
Gate! Gate! Paragate, Parasamgate, Bodhi Svaha!

When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, the monks, the Bodhisattvas, and all the gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others of the world, hearing the Buddha's words, rejoiced greatly and faithfully received and practiced them.

blocks.text: 4. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra

inline.s: Translated by the Tripitaka master Prajna together with Liyan and others of the land of Kashmir.

Thus I have heard. At one time the Buddha was dwelling at Vulture Peak Mountain in Rajagriha, together with a great assembly of monks and a multitude of Bodhisattvas. At that time the Buddha, the World-Honored One, entered into a samādhi named Extensive and Profound.

At that time, in the midst of the assembly there was a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva named Avalokiteshvara. When he practiced the profound Prajna Paramita, he illuminated the five aggregates and saw that they were empty, freeing himself from all suffering and distress. Immediately, Sariputra, by the power of the Buddha, joined his palms and reverently asked the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Good man, if one wishes to study the practice of the profound Prajna Paramita, how should he practice? Having thus asked

At that time the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara said to the venerable elder Sariputra: Sariputra, when a good man or good woman practices the profound Prajna Paramita, he should contemplate that the five aggregates are empty in their nature.
Sariputra, form is not other than emptiness, emptiness is not other than form; form is emptiness, emptiness is form. The same holds for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Sariputra, all dharmas are marked with emptiness; they neither arise nor cease, are neither defiled nor pure, neither increase nor decrease. Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental object; no realm of sight, up to no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance, and no extinction of ignorance; up to no aging and death, and no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, origination, cessation, or path; no wisdom; and no attainment.

Therefore, know that Prajna Paramita is the great god-mantra, the great illuminating mantra, the supreme mantra, the unequaled mantra, which can remove all suffering — this is true, not false. Therefore, the mantra of Prajna Paramita is proclaimed, and the mantra says:

Thus, Sariputra, all Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas should thus practice in the profound Prajna Paramita. Having thus spoken

Immediately, the World-Honored One rose from the samādhi of the Extensive and Profound and praised the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Well done! Well done! Good man, so it is, so it is. As you have said, one should thus practice the profound Prajna Paramita. When one practices thus, all Tathagatas rejoice. At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken these words, the venerable elder Sariputra was filled with great joy, and the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara likewise greatly rejoiced. At that time the gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others of that assembly, hearing the Buddha's words, rejoiced greatly and faithfully received and practiced them.

blocks.text: 5. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra

inline.s: Translated by imperial command by the Tripitaka monk Zhihuilun of the Great Xingshan Monastery in the Tang capital.

Thus I have heard. At one time the Bhagavan dwelt at Vulture Peak Mountain in Rajagriha, together with a great assembly of monks and a great multitude of Bodhisattvas. At that time the World-Honored One entered into a samādhi named the Extensive and Profound Illuminating Sight.

At that time, in the assembly there was a Bodhisattva-Mahasattva named Avalokiteshvara. When he practiced the profound Prajna Paramita, he illuminated the five aggregates, seeing that their self-nature was all empty. Immediately, the venerable elder Sariputra, by the Buddha's majestic power, joined his palms and reverently asked the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Holy One, if one wishes to study the practice of the profound Prajna Paramita, how should one practice? Having thus asked

At that time the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara told the venerable elder Sariputra: Sariputra, when a good man or good woman practices the profound Prajna Paramita, he should illuminate the five aggregates and see that their self-nature is all empty, free from all suffering and distress.

Sariputra, form is empty, and in the nature of emptiness form is seen; form is not other than emptiness, emptiness is not other than form; this form is emptiness, this emptiness is form. The same holds for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Sariputra, the nature and characteristics of all dharmas are empty; they neither arise nor cease, are neither defiled nor pure, neither decrease nor increase. Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental object; no realm of sight, up to no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance, and no extinction of ignorance; up to no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, origination, cessation, or path; no wisdom; and no realized attainment.

Because there is nothing to be attained, the Bodhisattva dwells relying on Prajna Paramita, and his mind is without obstruction. Because his mind is without obstruction, there is no fear; having distanced himself from inverted dreams and views, he reaches ultimate stillness.
The Buddhas of the three times, relying on Prajna Paramita, attained Anuttara Samyak Sambodhi and realized perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, know that Prajna Paramita is the great true dharani, the great illuminating dharani, the supreme dharani, the unequaled dharani, which can remove all suffering — this is true, not false.
Therefore, the true dharani of Prajna Paramita is proclaimed, and the dharani says:
Om (prolonged) ga-te ga-te, pa-ra (prolonged) ga-te, pa-ra (prolonged) sam-ga-te, bo-dhi sva (joined) ha (prolonged).
Thus, Sariputra, all Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas should thus train in the profound Prajna Paramita.

At that time the World-Honored One rose calmly from the samādhi and praised the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Well done! Well done! Good man, so it is, so it is. As you have said, one should thus practice the profound Prajna Paramita. When one practices thus, all Tathagatas rejoice.

At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken thus, the venerable elder Sariputra, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, and that whole assembly, together with all the gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas [horse
dog] among the worlds, hearing the Buddha's words, all rejoiced greatly and faithfully received and practiced them.

blocks.text: 6. The Heart of Prajna Paramita Sutra

inline.s: Translated by the national great virtue, the Tripitaka Master, the monk Facheng.

Thus I have heard. At one time the Bhagavan dwelt at Vulture Peak Mountain in Rajagriha, together with a great assembly of monks and all the Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas. At that time the World-Honored One entered into the samādhi of the profound and luminous Dharma, the door of distinction. And at that time the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara, practicing the profound Prajna Paramita, contemplated and illuminated the five aggregates, seeing that their essential nature was all empty.

At that time the venerable elder Sariputra, by the Buddha's majestic power, asked the holy Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Good man, if one wishes to train in the profound Prajna Paramita, how should he practice and study? Having thus spoken

The Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara answered the venerable elder Sariputra: If a good man or good woman wishes to train in the profound Prajna Paramita, he should contemplate thus: the essential nature of the five aggregates is all empty; form is emptiness, emptiness is form; form is not other than emptiness, emptiness is not other than form. Likewise, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are all likewise empty.

Therefore, Sariputra, all dharmas have the nature of emptiness and are without characteristics; they neither arise nor cease, are neither defiled nor free from defilement, neither decrease nor increase. Sariputra, therefore, within the nature of emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousness; no eye, no ear, no nose, no tongue, no body, no mind; no form, no sound, no smell, no taste, no touch, no mental object; no realm of sight, up to no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance, and no extinction of ignorance; up to no aging and death, and no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, origination, cessation, or path; no wisdom; no attainment, and also no non-attainment.

Therefore, Sariputra, because there is nothing to be attained, all the Bodhisattvas rely on Prajna Paramita, and their minds are without obstruction and without fear. Having transcended all inversion, they reach ultimate Nirvāṇa.
All the Buddhas of the three times, likewise relying on Prajna Paramita, realized the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Sariputra, therefore, know that the great secret mantra of Prajna Paramita is the great illuminating mantra, the supreme mantra, the unequaled mantra, the mantra that can remove all suffering, and it is true and without error. Therefore, know that Prajna Paramita is the secret mantra; now the mantra of Prajna Paramita is proclaimed:
Gate! Gate! Paragate, Parasamgate, Bodhi Svaha!
Sariputra, all Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas should thus train in the profound Prajna Paramita.

At that time the World-Honored One rose from that concentration and said to the holy Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Well done! Well done! Good man, so it is, so it is. As you have said, one should thus train in Prajna Paramita, and all Tathagatas will rejoice.

At that time, after the Bhagavan had spoken these words, the venerable elder Sariputra, the holy Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara, and all the gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others of the world, hearing the Buddha's words, all rejoiced greatly and faithfully received and practiced them.

blocks.text: 7. The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Prajna Paramita of the Holy Buddha-Mother

inline.s: Translated by imperial command by the Tripitaka master of the Western Regions, the Grand Master Dharmapala, the acting Minister of the Glorious Banquet, the Dharma-Transmitting Great Master bestowed with the purple robe, the Minister Shihu.

Thus I have heard. At one time the World-Honored One was at Vulture Peak Mountain in Rajagriha, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and surrounded by the host of Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas.

At that time the World-Honored One entered into the samādhi of the profound light that proclaims the true Dharma. At that time the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara was in the Buddha's assembly. This Bodhisattva-Mahasattva, already able to practice the profound Prajna Paramita, contemplated and saw that the five aggregates are empty in their self-nature.

At that time the venerable Sariputra, by the Buddha's majestic power, came forward and asked the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: If good men and good women are delighted to study this profound Prajna Paramita Dharma-gate, how should they study it?

At that time the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara told the venerable Sariputra: Listen attentively now, and I shall proclaim it for you. If good men and good women are delighted to study this profound Prajna Paramita Dharma-gate, they should contemplate the five aggregates, seeing that their self-nature is all empty. What is meant by the self-nature of the five aggregates being empty? It means that form is emptiness, emptiness is form; form is no different from emptiness, emptiness is no different from form. The same holds for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Sariputra, all these dharmas have such an empty mark: there is nothing that arises, nothing that ceases; no defilement, no purity; no increase, no decrease. Sariputra, therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental object; no realm of sight, no realm of eye-consciousness, up to no realm of mind, no realm of mental consciousness; no ignorance, no extinction of ignorance; up to no aging and death, and no extinction of aging and death; no suffering, origination, cessation, or path; no wisdom; no attainment, and also no non-attainment.

Sariputra, because of this non-attainment, the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva, relying on the practice corresponding to Prajna Paramita, has a mind with nothing to cling to and no obstruction. Because there is nothing to cling to and no obstruction, there is no fear; having distanced himself from all inverted views and false imaginings, he reaches ultimate perfect tranquility.
All the Buddhas of the three times, relying on this Prajna Paramita, attained Anuttara Samyak Sambodhi.

Therefore, one should know that Prajna Paramita is the vast illumination, the supreme illumination, the unequaled illumination, and it can quell and remove all affliction and suffering; this is the true Dharma without falsehood. All who study should thus train.
Now I shall proclaim the great illumination of Prajna Paramita:
ta[dya

tha] (tadyatha, one measure) Om (prolonged) ga-te (prolonged) ga-te (prolonged, two) pa-ra (prolonged) ga-te (prolonged, three) pa-ra (prolonged) sam-ga-te (prolonged, four) bo-dhi (prolonged) sva (prolonged) ha (prolonged, five).
Sariputra, if all Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas can recite these illuminating lines of Prajna Paramita, this is to train in the profound Prajna Paramita.

At that time the World-Honored One rose calmly from the samādhi and praised the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara: Well done! Well done! Good man, as you have said, so it is, so it is. Prajna Paramita should thus be studied; this is the true, supreme, and ultimate thing, and all Tathagatas rejoice.

When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva Avalokiteshvara, all the monks, and all the great assembly — the gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others of the world — hearing the Buddha's words, rejoiced greatly and faithfully received and practiced them.
